mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.2% signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital flows into risk assets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline return distribution).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 9.5% indicates severe labor market distress, reducing consumer spending capacity and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >40% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 93) and housing starts (HOUST < 600) signals a manufacturing and construction sector contraction, reducing GDP growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >50% of instances meeting INDPRO < 93 AND HOUST < 600 (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: Inflation exceeding 3.0% year-over-year (CPIAUCSL > 3.0) triggers central bank rate hikes, increasing real discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 600 thousand (HOUST > 600) indicate robust construction activity, signaling consumer confidence and rising GDP growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >45% of instances when HOUST > 600 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.2%) combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%) creates an optimal environment for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >50% of instances meeting FEDFUNDS < 0.2 AND CPIAUCSL < 2.5 (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Rising private payrolls (PAYEMS > 130,000) combined with strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 350,000) indicate labor market strength and consumption growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >45% of instances meeting PAYEMS > 130000 AND RSAFS > 350000 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 90 (INDPRO < 90) signals manufacturing sector weakness, reducing corporate output and earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when INDPRO < 90 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative return expectation).
